=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .github/workflows/clarify.yml (and similarly in .github/workflows/plan.yml, .github/workflows/implement.yml, .github/workflows/validate.yml, .github/workflows/orchestrate_clarify_respond.yml): stage_resolver_ref() function (lines ~76-87 in clarify.yml) | severity=medium | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v3_2, google_gemini-3-flash-preview, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, stepfun_step-3_5-flash]
  PROBLEM: Git command errors are suppressed with `--quiet`, making resolver-loading failures hard to debug.
  WHY: If `git init`, `fetch`, or `checkout` fails due to network, auth, or ref issues, the error is hidden and operators only see a generic fallback warning.
- .github/workflows/clarify.yml (and other workflow files) | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v3_2, google_gemini-3-flash-preview, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, stepfun_step-3_5-flash]
  PROBLEM: Temporary staging directories are not cleaned up after successful execution.
  WHY: The workflow leaves `resolver_stage_root` under `RUNNER_TEMP`, which can accumulate across runs and waste disk space, especially on long-lived/self-hosted runners.
- .github/workflows/clarify.yml (and other 4 workflow files) | severity=medium | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v3_2, google_gemini-3-flash-preview, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, stepfun_step-3_5-flash]
  PROBLEM: The fallback warning message misattributes resolver load failures to the ref being "unavailable".
  WHY: Git failures can stem from network, authentication, permissions, or repository access problems, so the current warning obscures the real cause.
- scripts/resolve_integration_ref.sh when executed from staged location | severity=medium | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v3_2, google_gemini-3-flash-preview, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5]
  PROBLEM: `REPO_ROOT` derivation breaks when the script runs from the staged directory.
  WHY: `SCRIPT_DIR` points at the staged checkout location, so `REPO_ROOT` no longer resolves the original repository tree and `--self-test` fixture lookup can fail.
- .github/workflows/clarify.yml (and other 4 workflow files) | severity=medium | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v3_2, google_gemini-3-flash-preview, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5]
  PROBLEM: `GH_TOKEN` is used to build the remote URL without validation that it is set.
  WHY: If the token is missing or empty, fetch authentication fails and the generic fallback hides a configuration problem.
- .github/workflows/clarify.yml (and the other four workflows) | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v3_2, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, stepfun_step-3_5-flash]
  PROBLEM: There is no explicit verification that `FETCH_HEAD` exists before `git checkout FETCH_HEAD`.
  WHY: The code relies on the `&&` chain alone, so an edge-case fetch/state mismatch could produce an unclear checkout failure instead of an explicit guard.
- tests/test_workflow_checkout_integration_ref_audit.py | severity=low | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v3_2]
  PROBLEM: The test is brittle because it asserts exact command strings rather than contract behavior.
  WHY: Benign implementation changes such as adding `--no-tags` or adjusting quoting would fail the test even if the resolver contract remains correct.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v3_2 ===
- .github/workflows/clarify.yml (and similarly in .github/workflows/plan.yml, .github/workflows/implement.yml, .github/workflows/validate.yml, .github/workflows/orchestrate_clarify_respond.yml): stage_resolver_ref() function (lines ~76-87 in clarify.yml) | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Git command errors are suppressed with `--quiet`, making resolver-loading failures difficult to debug
  WHY: If `git init`, fetch, or checkout fails due to network issues, authentication problems, or permissions, the error is hidden and only a generic "unavailable" warning is shown. Operators cannot diagnose the root cause.
- .github/workflows/clarify.yml (and other workflow files) | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Temporary staging directories are not cleaned up after successful execution
  WHY: While each run creates a unique directory, failed or interrupted runs may leave directories accumulating on the runner, consuming disk space over time.
- .github/workflows/clarify.yml (and other workflow files)  
  PROBLEM: Warning message mischaracterizes git failures as "unavailable" refs
  WHY: Git failures could be due to network timeouts, authentication errors, rate limits, or repository access issues, not just unavailable refs. Misleading messages waste debugging time.
- scripts/resolve_integration_ref.sh when executed from staged location
  PROBLEM: REPO_ROOT derivation breaks when script runs from staged directory
  WHY: Self-test mode depends on finding tests/fixtures/integration_ref_resolver relative to REPO_ROOT. When script is staged from another repo, SCRIPT_DIR points to staged location, not actual repo root.
- .github/workflows/clarify.yml (and other 4 workflow files)
  PROBLEM: No verification that FETCH_HEAD exists before checkout
  WHY: If git fetch fails but returns 0 (e.g., cached result, network timeout), or if stale FETCH_HEAD exists, checkout may operate on invalid or unrelated data.
- .github/workflows/clarify.yml (and other 4 workflow files)
  PROBLEM: No validation that GH_TOKEN is set before using it in git remote URL
  WHY: If GH_TOKEN is empty or unset, git commands will fail with authentication errors but the error message will be suppressed (see issue 1).
- tests/test_workflow_checkout_integration_ref_audit.py
  PROBLEM: Test is brittle - asserts exact command strings rather than contract compliance
  WHY: Benign implementation changes (e.g., adding --no-tags to git fetch) will cause test failures even though the resolver contract is maintained.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v3_2 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3-flash-preview ===
- scripts/resolve_integration_ref.sh | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The script incorrectly derives the repository root when executed from its staged location in `${RUNNER_TEMP}`.
  WHY: When the workflow stages the resolver repo into `${RUNNER_TEMP}/integration-ref-resolver-.../primary`, `SCRIPT_DIR` becomes `.../primary/scripts`. `REPO_ROOT` then becomes `.../primary`. However, the self-test mode (`--self-test`) relies on `FIXTURE_DIR="${REPO_ROOT}/tests/fixtures/..."`. If the staging process is a shallow fetch of only specific paths (though here it currently checkouts the whole ref), any deviation from the expected repo structure or running from a temp directory breaks the path to fixtures. While the current `stage_resolver_ref` function fetches the full ref, relying on `REPO_ROOT` to find test fixtures during a runtime-staged execution is fragile.
- .github/workflows/clarify.yml (and other 4 workflow files) | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Lack of cleanup for temporary directories.
  WHY: The `resolver_stage_root` is created using `${GITHUB_RUN_ID}-${GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT}`. While these are unique per run, they are created in `${RUNNER_TEMP}`. GitHub-hosted runners usually clean this up, but on self-hosted runners or long-lived environments, these directories will accumulate, wasting disk space.
- .github/workflows/clarify.yml (and other 4 workflow files) | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Undocumented dependency on `GH_TOKEN` in the environment.
  WHY: The shell function `stage_resolver_ref` uses `resolver_remote_url`, which expands `${GH_TOKEN}`. If the step environment does not explicitly map `GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}`, the git fetch will fail with an authentication error. The current PR does not show the `env:` block for the modified step to confirm if this mapping was added.
- .github/workflows/clarify.yml (and other 4 workflow files) | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Silent failure suppression in `stage_resolver_ref`.
  WHY: By using `--quiet` and capturing the result in an `if` block that `rm -rf` the directory on failure, any network errors, ref-not-found errors, or git-init issues are completely hidden. The user only sees "Resolver support ref ... is unavailable", which is misleading if the actual cause is a transient network blip or an auth failure.
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3-flash-preview ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===
- .github/workflows/clarify.yml (and .github/workflows/plan.yml, .github/workflows/implement.yml, .github/workflows/validate.yml, .github/workflows/orchestrate_clarify_respond.yml) | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: All git commands use `--quiet` flags that suppress error output, making resolver-loading failures difficult to debug
  WHY: When `git init`, `git remote add`, `git fetch`, or `git checkout` fail due to network issues, authentication problems, or invalid refs, the error messages are silently discarded. The caller only sees "ref is unavailable" which obscures the root cause
- .github/workflows/clarify.yml (and sibling workflow files) | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The temporary staging directory `${RUNNER_TEMP}/integration-ref-resolver-${GITHUB_RUN_ID}-${GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT}` is created but never explicitly cleaned up after execution
  WHY: Over multiple workflow runs, temp directories accumulate in `${RUNNER_TEMP}`. While runner environments are typically ephemeral, this causes unnecessary disk growth and makes debugging harder when examining runner state
- .github/workflows/clarify.yml (and sibling workflow files) | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Warning says "Resolver support ref ${resolver_ref} is unavailable" but actual failure could be due to network issues, authentication errors, git configuration problems, or repository access issues
  WHY: Operators debugging resolver loading failures receive misleading error context - the ref may exist but fetch failed due to other reasons
- scripts/resolve_integration_ref..sh | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Script calculates `REPO_ROOT` as `${SCRIPT_DIR}/..`. When executed from staged location (`${RUNNER_TEMP}/integration-ref-resolver-*/primary/scripts/`), `REPO_ROOT` points to the staging directory, not the actual repository. The `FIXTURE_DIR` path becomes invalid.
  WHY: The script's `--self-test` mode will fail if invoked from the staged location (low severity - self-test is development-only, not production)
- .github/workflows/clarify.yml (and sibling workflow files) | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Code constructs git remote URL with `GH_TOKEN` but does not validate the token is present. If `GH_TOKEN` is empty or undefined, the URL becomes malformed (`https://x-access-token:@host/repo`) and git authentication will fail.
  WHY: While the workflow passes `GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GH_PAT }}` via env, if that mapping is ever missed, the failure message will be misleading (git will report authentication failure, not "token missing")
- tests/test_workflow_checkout_integration_ref_audit.py | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Test asserts literal strings like `git -C "${dest}" fetch --quiet --depth 1 origin "${ref}"`. Future improvements to the git command (adding retries, changing depth, etc.) will break the test even if the security contract remains satisfied.
  WHY: Test brittleness - developers may avoid legitimate improvements or the test will fail on benign changes
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===
